**Context.** Research Intern at General Intelligence Machine (GIM), Summer 2026 – present.

**What it is.** RoboChrono asks vision-language models seven questions about a live robot
stream, under a causal protocol (only frames up to time *t* are visible): what is the robot
doing now, what comes next, which frame or view matches, in what order did things happen,
and when did an action start and end. The data comes from two real dual-arm platforms,
collected via VR teleoperation with synchronized head and wrist cameras, and is annotated
by humans into action and state intervals.

**My part.** I led the VR-teleop data collection on GIM's dual-arm whole-workspace platform,
designed the annotation and QA-template protocol, built the VLM evaluation harness used for
the 18-model sweep, and led the results analysis. I also contributed to scenario design,
camera synchronization, the input ablations, and the Hugging Face release.

**Why it matters.** The best frontier model scores 80.5% on average but drops to 68.3% on
frame ordering, and removing vision barely hurts next-action prediction. VLMs still lean on
task priors rather than on what they see, which is exactly the failure mode a robot cannot
afford.

Paper: [arXiv 2609.36605](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36605) ·
